data.why: constants.py ships a hardcoded default protein sequence (SARS-CoV-2 spike) that pre-fills the text area on load; there is no file upload in this app, only a text box, so no sample files are needed.

goals: Digest a protein sequence in silico with a chosen protease (e.g. trypsin) and see the resulting tryptic peptides
Tune missed cleavages, peptide length and mass filters to match a mass-spec search's parameters
Check what fraction of the protein sequence is covered by the generated peptide list, and how coverage changes with missed cleavages, length or mass cutoffs
Predict which peptides are proteotypic (likely to be observed) and filter out peptides unlikely to be detected
Search for a sequence motif (e.g. N-glycosylation site N[ST][^P]) and see which peptides contain it and how it maps onto the protein coverage plot
Fetch a protein sequence directly from UniProt by accession number instead of pasting it

review.summary: The tree covers what the README says Protein Cleaver is for: digesting proteins, filtering peptides, predicting which are proteotypic, checking coverage and searching motifs. All 13 screens I checked match their nodes. It needs light restructuring before filing: the input phase favours the demo, phase 2 mixes modifications into cutting rules, and the UniProt fetch, RT, export and link-out steps are missing; one reported bug is contradicted by the replay and another the check found is left out.
